exposure: severity of sexual violence (mild, moderate, severe/rape)
cohort: 74,059 pregnant women enrolled in the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study between 1999 and 2008
finding: Women with a history of rape had higher odds of elective caesarean section and induction and significantly fewer episiotomies.
mod_finding: Severe sexual violence (rape) was associated with elective caesarean section, while moderate sexual violence was associated with an increased risk of emergency caesarean section; no association was found between sexual violence and operative vaginal birth, except for a lower risk among multiparous women reporting mild sexual violence.
